stem: What is an **ore**?

options.content: a rock with enough metal compound for extraction to make a profit
options.rationale: Grade, value and cost decide whether a rock is an ore.

options.content: a pure metal found as lumps in the ground
options.rationale: That is a native metal.

options.content: any rock that contains some metal or a metal compound in it
options.rationale: Many rocks contain metals in amounts too small to extract profitably.

options.content: the waste rock left behind after extraction
options.rationale: Waste rock is gangue (or tailings).

explanation: An ore is a rock from which a metal can be extracted at a profit. A rock containing a little metal is not an ore unless extraction pays.

stem: Which two minerals are ores of **iron**?

options.rationale: These are ores of copper and nickel (both also contain iron, but are mined for Cu and Ni).
These are ores of chromium and aluminium.
Fe₂O₃ and Fe₃O₄.
These are lithium ores.

explanation: Iron is extracted from oxide ores: haematite (Fe₂O₃) and magnetite (Fe₃O₄).

stem: True or false: any rock that contains a metal compound is an ore.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Not quite: a rock is an ore only if the metal can be extracted from it at a profit.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: Correct: an ore must contain enough of the metal for extraction to be profitable.

explanation: Many rocks contain small amounts of metal compounds. A rock is an ore only when the metal can be extracted from it at a profit, which depends on the grade, the value of the metal and the cost of mining and processing.

stem: What is the formula of the iron ore **magnetite**?

options.rationale: This is iron pyrite, a sulfide.
Magnetite is magnetic, which helps separate it.
This is haematite.
This is iron(II) oxide, not magnetite.

explanation: Magnetite is Fe₃O₄, a magnetic iron oxide. Haematite is Fe₂O₃.

stem: Chalcopyrite, $\ce{CuFeS2}$, is mined as an ore of which metal?

options.rationale: It contains iron, but it is mined for its copper.
Chalcopyrite (copper pyrites) is the main copper ore.
Nickel's main ore is pentlandite.
Gold is found native.

explanation: Chalcopyrite, also called copper pyrites, is a copper iron sulfide and the most important ore of copper.

stem: Match each ore mineral with the metal it is mined for.
explanation: Chromite (FeCr₂O₄) – chromium; pentlandite ((Fe,Ni)₉S₈) – nickel; petalite (LiAlSi₄O₁₀) – lithium; chalcopyrite (CuFeS₂) – copper. Aluminium comes from bauxite.

stem: The Great Dyke in Zimbabwe is best known for deposits of which minerals?

options.rationale: These lithium minerals occur in pegmatites elsewhere.
These are associated with aluminium, not the Great Dyke.
Chromite seams and a PGM-bearing layer run along the Dyke.
Zimbabwe's main coal field is at Hwange, not on the Great Dyke.

explanation: The Great Dyke, a long band of igneous rock through central Zimbabwe, contains chromite and the platinum-group metals (with nickel and copper).

stem: Why is gold found as the native metal, while iron is found as compounds such as haematite?

options.content: Gold is more reactive than iron in the ground.
options.rationale: Gold is far less reactive than iron.

options.content: Iron is too heavy to stay as a metal in rocks.
options.rationale: Density has nothing to do with it.

options.content: Gold is formed slowly from iron in the rocks over millions of years.
options.rationale: Elements do not change into other elements in rocks.

options.content: Gold is very unreactive, but iron reacts to form compounds.
options.rationale: Reactive metals are found combined; unreactive metals can be found native.

explanation: Gold is near the bottom of the reactivity series, so it stays uncombined. Iron is more reactive and has combined with oxygen to form oxide ores.

stem: Name **one** lithium ore mineral.

rejected.feedback: Name the mineral (the ore), not the metal.
Bauxite is the ore of aluminium.

explanation: Lithium is extracted from silicate minerals such as petalite (LiAlSi₄O₁₀), spodumene (LiAlSi₂O₆) and lepidolite (a lithium mica).

stem: Chromite has the formula FeCr₂O₄. Calculate the percentage by mass of chromium in chromite, to 3 significant figures. (Ar: O = 16, Cr = 52, Fe = 56)
explanation: $M_r(\ce{FeCr2O4}) = 56 + 2 \times 52 + 4 \times 16 = 224$. Percentage of chromium $= \dfrac{104}{224} \times 100 = 46.4\%$.
hints: There are two chromium atoms in each formula unit.

stem: Spodumene has the formula LiAlSi₂O₆. Calculate the percentage by mass of lithium in spodumene, to 3 significant figures. (Ar: Li = 7, O = 16, Al = 27, Si = 28)
explanation: $M_r(\ce{LiAlSi2O6}) = 7 + 27 + 2 \times 28 + 6 \times 16 = 186$. Percentage of lithium $= \dfrac{7}{186} \times 100 = 3.76\%$.
hints: Add up the masses of all ten atoms in the formula.

stem: A sample of iron ore contains 64.0% haematite, Fe₂O₃, by mass. The rest is gangue. (Ar: O = 16, Fe = 56)

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the percentage by mass of iron in haematite.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the maximum mass of iron, in tonnes, in 5.00 tonnes of the ore.
parts.workedSolution:
1. Mass of $\ce{Fe2O3} = 5.00 \times 0.640 = 3.20$ t.
2. Mass of iron $= 3.20 \times 0.700 = 2.24$ t.

parts.label: (c)

points.description: The unwanted rock/minerals mixed with the valuable mineral in an ore

parts.explanation: Gangue is the worthless rock and minerals mixed with the valuable mineral; it has to be separated off and disposed of.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Some iron ores contain magnetite, Fe₃O₄, instead of haematite. Which property of magnetite helps to separate it from gangue?

options.rationale: Magnetite is insoluble.

options.content: It is a liquid at room temperature.
options.rationale: Magnetite is a solid.
This does not help to separate it.
Magnets can pull crushed magnetite away from the waste rock.

explanation: $M_r(\ce{Fe2O3}) = 160$, of which $112$ is iron: $70.0\%$. The ore contains $5.00 \times 0.640 = 3.20$ t of haematite, which contains $3.20 \times 0.700 = 2.24$ t of iron.
hints: First find the mass of haematite in the ore.

stem: What type of compound are chalcopyrite, $\ce{CuFeS2}$, and pentlandite, $\ce{(Fe,Ni)9S8}$?

options.rationale: They contain no carbonate ions.
They contain no oxygen.
They contain no silicon or oxygen.
They contain metals combined with sulfur only.

explanation: Both minerals are metal sulfides. Sulfide ores are usually concentrated and then roasted or smelted, which produces sulfur dioxide.
hints: Look at the non-metal in each formula.

stem: A rock contains 0.5% copper. Whether it is worth mining as a copper ore depends mainly on:

options.content: the colour and appearance of the rock
options.rationale: Colour does not decide whether extraction is profitable.

options.content: the copper price and the cost of mining and processing
options.rationale: An ore must be profitable to extract.

options.content: whether the rock is magnetic or not
options.rationale: Magnetism may help processing, but profit is the deciding factor.

options.content: whether copper is classed as a metal or as a non-metal
options.rationale: Copper is always a metal; the question is whether extraction pays.

explanation: Whether a rock is an ore is an economic question: the value of the metal that can be recovered must be greater than the cost of mining, processing and transport.
hints: What does the word 'ore' imply about profit?

stem: Complete the sentences about ores.

payload.template: Haematite is iron(III) {{blank:a}}. Magnetite can be separated from waste rock because it is {{blank:b}}. Gold occurs in rocks as the {{blank:c}} metal.

explanation: Haematite is Fe₂O₃ (an oxide); magnetite (Fe₃O₄) is magnetic; gold occurs native (as the uncombined metal).

stem: In one deposit, the ore contains 3.5 g of platinum-group metals (PGMs) in each tonne of rock. Calculate the mass of ore, in tonnes, that must be mined and processed to obtain 1.00 kg of PGMs. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
explanation: $1.00\ \text{kg} = 1000\ \text{g}$. Mass of ore $= \dfrac{1000}{3.5} = 285.7 \approx 286$ tonnes. Only a very valuable metal is worth extracting at such a low grade.
workedSolution:
1. $1.00\ \text{kg} = 1000\ \text{g}$ of PGMs.
2. Each tonne gives $3.5\ \text{g}$, so tonnes needed $= 1000 \div 3.5 = 285.7$.
3. To 3 s.f.: $286$ tonnes.

stem: Platinum is mined from rock containing only a few grams of the metal per tonne, but iron ore must contain a large percentage of iron to be worth mining. Explain why. [4]

points.description: An ore must be profitable: the value of the metal recovered must exceed the cost of extraction
Platinum is very rare and valuable (high price per gram)
So even a few grams per tonne are worth more than the cost of mining and processing the rock
Iron has a low price per tonne, so a low-grade iron ore would cost more to process than the iron is worth

answerSpec.modelAnswer: A rock is only an ore if the metal can be extracted at a profit. Platinum is rare and extremely valuable, so even a few grams of platinum in a tonne of rock are worth more than the cost of mining, crushing and processing that tonne. Iron is cheap, so the iron obtained from a tonne of rock is worth relatively little; unless the rock contains a large percentage of iron, processing it would cost more than the iron is worth.

explanation: Whether a rock is an ore depends on the balance between the value of the metal and the cost of extracting it.
hints: Compare the value of each metal with the cost of processing a tonne of rock.

stem: Which mineral contains the **highest** percentage by mass of the metal it is mined for? (Ar: O = 16, S = 32, Cr = 52, Fe = 56, Cu = 64)

options.rationale: 112 ÷ 160 × 100 = 70.0% iron: slightly less than magnetite.

explanation: Calculate each percentage: magnetite 72.4% Fe, haematite 70.0% Fe, chromite 46.4% Cr, chalcopyrite 34.8% Cu. Magnetite is the highest.
hints: Work out the percentage of the named metal in each formula.

stem: Pentlandite has the formula $\ce{(Fe,Ni)9S8}$. What does this formula show?

options.content: Iron and nickel share nine metal atoms per eight S, in varying amounts.
options.rationale: Nickel and iron share the metal positions in the crystal.

options.content: It is a mixture of iron metal, nickel metal and sulfur.
options.rationale: It is a compound (a sulfide mineral), not a mixture of elements.

options.content: It contains no sulfur, only iron and nickel.
options.rationale: S is the symbol for sulfur.

options.content: It contains exactly nine iron atoms and eight nickel atoms in each unit.
options.rationale: The 9 refers to iron and nickel together; the 8 refers to sulfur.

explanation: The bracket (Fe,Ni) means that iron and nickel can replace each other in the crystal, so their ratio varies, but there are always nine metal atoms to eight sulfur atoms.
hints: What does the comma inside the bracket mean?

stem: True or false: chromite, an ore of chromium, is found on the Great Dyke.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Correct: the Great Dyke contains major chromite deposits as well as platinum-group metals.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: It is true: chromite seams run along the Great Dyke.

explanation: Chromite (FeCr₂O₄) occurs in seams along the Great Dyke. It is smelted into ferrochrome for stainless steel.

stem: An ore contains 20.0% petalite, LiAlSi₄O₁₀, by mass. Calculate the maximum mass of lithium, in kg, in 1.00 tonne (1000 kg) of the ore. (Ar: Li = 7, O = 16, Al = 27, Si = 28)
explanation: Mass of petalite $= 0.200 \times 1000 = 200\ \text{kg}$. $M_r(\ce{LiAlSi4O10}) = 306$, so lithium $= 200 \times \dfrac{7}{306} = 4.58\ \text{kg}$.
workedSolution:
1. Mass of petalite $= 20.0\% \times 1000 = 200\ \text{kg}$. **(M1)**
2. $M_r = 7 + 27 + 4 \times 28 + 10 \times 16 = 306$.
3. Mass of lithium $= 200 \times \dfrac{7}{306} = 4.575 \approx 4.58\ \text{kg}$. **(A1)**
hints: Find the mass of petalite in the ore first.
Then find the fraction of lithium in petalite.
